## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The timestamp semantics and NULL documentation should be corrected because they misrepresent process completion and prior start history.

## Changes
The pull request adds `finished_at` to the latest-event process model and documents the column in the schema catalog. It also adds `review.txt`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- models/processes.sql:10 — correctness — A started process receives a finish timestamp — For process 20, whose only event is `started`, `finished_at` receives its start timestamp despite models/schema.yml:11 specifying “Timestamp when the process finished.” The CASE selects initiation as completion. — Consumers interpreting the documented completion timestamp will classify a process with only a start event as finished. — Fix: Establish whether this column represents starting or finishing, then align its name, predicate, and documentation.
- models/schema.yml:17 — comments — Correct the NULL description for previously started processes — For process 30, which has `started` followed by `cleared`, “NULL means the process has never been started” is false: `case when event_type = 'started' then occurred_at end` returns NULL for its latest event. — Consumers following this description will interpret missing timestamps as proof that previously started processes never started.
